tourism.detail: Tourism under 90 days. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

meetings.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
meetings.detail: Consulting with business associates is a permitted activity. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.
meetings.next: Be ready to explain the purpose at the border.

conference.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
conference.detail: Attending professional conferences is permitted. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

unpaid-speaking.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
unpaid-speaking.detail: Speaking at a conference without payment is generally a business visit; officers decide at the border. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.
unpaid-speaking.next: Carry the invitation showing no payment beyond expenses.

paid-speaking.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program (honorarium rules)
paid-speaking.detail: Speaking fees are allowed only from qualifying (mainly academic or nonprofit research) institutions, for no more than nine days at one institution and from no more than five institutions in six months; no salary from a US entity. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.
paid-speaking.next: Check the payer qualifies; otherwise a work visa is needed.

book-launch.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program or a work visa
book-launch.detail: Promotion and readings may be business activity; paid appearances fall under the honorarium limits. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.
book-launch.next: Ask a US Embassy or an immigration lawyer.

ai-teaching.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program (honorarium rules) or a work visa
ai-teaching.detail: Academic lectures can fit the honorarium rules; paid teaching for a company needs a work visa. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

remote-work.route: Not addressed for visitors (US immigration law)
remote-work.detail: Visitors (ESTA or B visa) may not take employment; the State Department pages list meetings, conferences and negotiations but do not address remote work for a foreign employer either way.
remote-work.next: Ask US Customs and Border Protection or a US consulate in writing.

entrepreneur.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
entrepreneur.detail: Negotiating contracts and meeting partners fit; working in a US business needs a visa. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

trade.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program
trade.detail: Contract negotiation is a permitted activity. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

artist.route: Performer visa (for example O or P)
artist.detail: Only amateurs taking part unpaid in musical or similar events fit the waiver. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

mixed-mission.detail: The waiver covers business visits only; any work needs a visa. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.

filming.route: Media (I) visa for foreign media work
filming.detail: Representatives of foreign film or other information media are excluded from B-1 business visits. US immigration law applies in the US Virgin Islands.
filming.next: Ask a US Embassy which visa fits the filming you plan.

research.route: B-1 or ESTA for independent research (US law applies)
research.detail: US immigration law applies here: independent, unpaid research benefiting no US institution is a permitted B-1 activity.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Cash declaration: United States federal rules (31 CFR 1010.340) require a report when more than US$10,000 in currency or monetary instruments is moved into or out of the United States at one time. US$10,000 is about A$14,205 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026 (A$1 = USD 0.7040). The text read doesn't say how it treats movements to and from a US territory, so confirm with US Customs and Border Protection before relying on it for this place.

items.text: The Virgin Islands Cannabis Use Act (Act 8680), signed on 18 January (the Government's page dated 16 March 2023), covers adult use, medicinal use and sacramental use. The Government House notice said simple possession is decriminalised, with a fine of $100 for up to 1 ounce, and that adult, medicinal and sacramental use stayed prohibited until the rules were finalised.
The notice says that once the rules are in force, public consumption and possession or consumption at federal facilities stay prohibited, as does carrying cannabis between islands.

The Governor signed off the rules and regulations for the Virgin Islands Cannabis Program, reported on 21 May 2024. The rules govern licences and vendors. Whether sales and adult use are operating today was not confirmed.

culture-cycles.public_holidays: US Virgin Islands legal holidays are set by Title 1 of the Virgin Islands Code, section 171, and the Governor may add days by proclamation. The Governor's 2025-26 proclamation lists Christmas Day (Thursday 25 December 2025) and Christmas Second Day (Friday 26 December 2025) among them. The 2026-27 and 2027 lists were not read.
festivals: Crucian Christmas Festival: the Governor's 2025-26 proclamation describes it as showing Virgin Islands culture, and grants non-essential government employees time off around it. Government offices may be closed on those days.
culture-cycles.note: Recheck the Governor's holiday proclamation for the 2026-27 season and Title 1 VIC section 171 for the 2027 list.
